prompt:
You are a "goldfish" critic: a fresh reader with no history of this project. Your persona is a skeptical architect who hates unnecessary complexity, speculative features (YAGNI) and fixes of symptoms instead of root causes. You are strictly read-only: do not edit, write or create any file, and do not run git commands that change anything. You may read files and run read-only commands.

The project is theOS, a standalone project in /home/user/maiacity/theOS/. Everything is built from scratch inside theOS/; code outside it is legacy and must not be changed or depended on.

Read only these four things:
1. The record: /home/user/maiacity/theOS/aip/aip-31df.json (its claims c2 and c4, checkpoint 2, gaps, and its latest events).
2. The decision that sets this checkpoint's scope: /home/user/maiacity/theOS/brain/decisions/d-5afb.json (check per view type, speed first, fine-tune later).
3. The diff of checkpoint 2's code: {diff} (theOS/avenCEO/checks/check.mjs and theOS/avenCEO/checks/fixtures/behind-button.html). The whole file theOS/avenCEO/checks/check.mjs may be read for context; checkpoint 1's code was reviewed in /home/user/maiacity/theOS/aip/aip-31df/c1-review.json (if that path does not exist, find c1-review under theOS/aip/), and its findings are settled.
{earlier}
Your job is the zoom-out review of this diff:
1. YAGNI: what in it is not needed for checkpoint 2 and its claims c2 and c4, within d-5afb's scope? What could be deleted?
2. Simplest form: is there a clearly simpler way to do the same thing, with the same result?
3. Root cause: does it make the crawl reach what a person can reach (c2), or is it tuned to the replay commits?
4. Correctness that would make the check lie: a pass where a person would see a problem, a failure where none is, or a reported coverage or time that is not true.

For each finding give: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), the place (file and line or function), and the reasoning, with a concrete simpler alternative where you have one. At most 500 words, plain text, no praise, lead with what is wrong. If you find no Blocker or Major, say so plainly.

findings.scope: aip-31df, claim c2 against the verified event
findings.text: c2 says the crawl reaches every state a person can reach; its check asks for every route the docs list and the Learn tabs at the two replay commits. The event reports 186 to 187 of 214 slides and OLD-AIP pages and the Learn tab on 9 of 23. That fails c2 as written; d-5afb accepted misses but didn't change c2. Change c2 to what the crawl promises, or record it as failing; don't mark it passed.
findings.note: Agreed: c2 is not marked passed. Its result records the numbers (now from the committed coverage.mjs: slides 96 to 98 of 123, OLD-AIP pages 91 of 91, Learn tabs 9 of 23, docs by id 334 of 334). Whether c2 is narrowed to what d-5afb gives (one state per view type) or the crawl must reach every route is Samuel's, asked at Gate B.

findings.text: The diff adds no time limit; c4 is measured once by hand, and the time went from 56 to 101 s inside this checkpoint. Nothing reports when it passes 300 s. Fail when report.seconds > 300.
findings.note: Fixed: LIMIT = 300 s; a run at or over it prints a FAIL line and exits 1.

findings.scope: pageView's window.__kind with data attribute names
findings.text: Tuned to the replays (the app's data-itab tabs), and it changes far more than buttons: __view feeds the state key, so any box with a data attribute splits view types, slower against d-5afb. Revert __kind to element and classes, or add the data attributes to the button kind only.
findings.note: Fixed the narrower way, after measuring it: data attribute names only in a button's kind, the view type back to element and classes. At 106ba0e5f's parent the Learn tab is reached on the same 9 of 23. Without either, it was reached on none, because a tab button counted as the same kind as the chapter buttons: a general miss (a button made a tab by its data attribute), not one commit's.

findings.text: Nothing in this AIP reads the screenshots (aip-f4e2 defers the pixel diff and the look checker), they nearly doubled the time (56 to 101 s), and they are viewport-only, so content below the fold is missing. Put them behind a flag off by default until aip-f4e2 says what it needs; the scope is Samuel's.
findings.note: Checkpoint 2, approved at Gate A, lists a screenshot of every state at both sizes, and c4's check names them (each taken after document.fonts.ready). Measured: they add about 35 s, and the run stays at 102 s, a third of c4's limit. Whether they are full page or viewport is aip-f4e2's, which reads them; Samuel sees them at Gate B.
